statement.p: Determine the global extreme values of the function f(x,y)=2x^{3}+2x^{2}y+4y^{2}, \quad x,y \ge 0, x+y \le 1

static.solution:
f_x(x,y)=6x^{2}+4xy=x\mathopen{}\left(6x+4y\right)=0 f_y(x,y)=2x^{2}+8y=0 The first equation gives x=0 or y=-1.5x.
Substituting x=0 in the second equation gives 8 y=0 or y=0.
We obtain the critical point (0,0). We now substitute y=-1.5x in the second equation and solve for x: 2x^{2}-12x=x\mathopen{}\left(2x-12\right)=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x=0, x=6 We get the critical points (0,0), (6,-9).
None of the critical points is in the interior of the domain.
We check the boundary. The boundary consists of the three segments \mathrm{OA},\mathrm{OB} and \mathrm{AB} shown in the figure.
We consider each part of the boundary separately.
The segment \mathrm{OA}: On this segment y=0, 0\le x\le 1, and f(x,y)=f(x,0)=2x^{3}.
The minimum value is f(0,0)=0 and the maximum value is f(1,0)=2.
The segment \mathrm{OB}: On this segment x=0, 0\le y\le 1, and f(x,y)=f(0,y)=4y^{2}.
The minimum value is f(0,0)=0 and the maximum value is f(1,0)=4.
The segment \mathrm{AB}: On this segment y=1-x, 0\le x\le 1, and f(x,1-x)=2x^{3}+2x^{2}\mathopen{}\left(1-x\right)+4\mathopen{}\left(1-x\right)^{2}=6x^{2}-8x+4
We find extreme values of g(x)=6x^{2}-8x+4 in the interval 0\le x\le 1.
Setting g'(x)=0 we find g'(x)=12x-8=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{4}{6} g\left(\frac{4}{6}\right)=1.33333, \quad g(0)=4, \quad g(1)=2
In conclusion, we find that the global minimum of f on the given domain is f_{min}=0 and the global maximum f_{max}=4
